audit.summary: The weak topology of random finite measures controls expected linear tests, not expected same-outcome self-products. The asserted truncated-energy convergence in Proposition 5.1 is false as an implication of the stated convergence and bounds. No counterexample to the dimension formula is claimed.
limitations: P1 — Counterevidence: The example preserves compactness, nonzero limiting mass, boundary support and uniform full energy. Its limiting measure has finite energy. It does not refute the prelimit energy estimate, the compactness theorem, the dimension formula, or an additional BRW-specific convergence lemma if separately proved. These random subsets are not asserted to be BRW traces.
Counterevidence: The desired weighted pair-count exponent 2n-k is compatible with correct geometry: k+2(n-k)=2n-k. Thus the same intended geometric energy ratio can survive the local correction.
Limitations: The entire 50-page preprint text was read; this is not full certification of every proof or external result.

proposition.claim:
In the proof of Proposition 5.1, bounded continuity of kappa wedge delta_hat^(-h) and weak convergence of random finite measures are used to infer convergence of expected double integrals against their same-outcome self-products.

X compact Floyd compactification of the free group F_2 with lambda=3/4 and isolated vertices. eta_n uniform on 2^n positive words of depth n; eta Bernoulli boundary measure. Z_n independent Bernoulli(1/2); chi_n=2 Z_n eta_n; chi=eta. Random masses bounded by 2; mean mass 1; Omega-marginals at most 2P; supports escape every finite vertex set. Same diagonal modification as p.30: delta_hat(x,x)=lambda^|x| at vertices, zero at boundary; h=1.
